usage: This is the most common word for family across the Levant, referring to both immediate and extended family depending on context. Another very common term is ahel, which usually refers to one's parents or immediate folks living in the same house. When greeting someone, it is standard to ask about their family as a polite formality.

variants.label: my family
variants.note: Used when talking about your own family.

variants.label: your family (to a man)
variants.note: Used when asking a male about his family.

variants.label: your family (to a woman)
variants.note: Used when asking a female about her family.

variants.label: my folks / parents
variants.note: Used specifically to refer to your parents or the immediate family you grew up with.

examples.english: Say hi to your folks for me.
